title: Shogayaki Ginger Pork with Cabbage
summary: A Japanese-style dinner of thin pork slices quickly fried in a savoury ginger-soy glaze, served with crisp shredded cabbage. It is fast, punchy and dairy-free, ideal for a weeknight meal with rice if you like.
steps: Put the shredded cabbage in a bowl of cold water for 5 minutes to crisp, then drain very well and pile it onto serving plates.
Mix the grated ginger, grated garlic, soy sauce, white wine and sugar in a small bowl until the sugar dissolves.
Pat the pork slices dry and season lightly with a pinch of salt and black pepper.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the sliced onion and cook for 2–3 minutes, stirring, until just softened and starting to colour at the edges.
Add the pork in a single layer as much as possible. Fry for 2–3 minutes, turning once, until the pork loses its pink colour and begins to brown lightly.
Pour in the ginger-soy sauce and toss the pork and onion through it. Cook for 2–3 minutes more, until the sauce is glossy, slightly reduced and coating the pork.
Serve the hot ginger pork and onions immediately alongside the crisp shredded cabbage, spooning any extra pan sauce over the pork.
